 Judgment

The appeal is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Senior Civil Judge and MACT at Kadur, Chikkamagalur District, vide judgment and award dated 01.01.2019 in M.V.C.No.23/2013.
2.
The factum of accident and injuries sustained by the claimant and coverage of insurance are not in dispute.
Heard the arguments from both sides and perused the materials on record.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant/claimant submitted that the claimant was 11 years old at the time of accident and has sustained grievous injuries to the head and right leg and due to which the claimant is suffering from neurological problems and is not able to do any activities and was forced to stop education at SSLC level.
Therefore, prays for enhancement of compensation.

5. It is submitted that from the evidence of doctors - CW-1 to CW-3 among whom one is Neurologist has stated that the total neurological disability is at 43.75% due to the injury to the head and 9%
towards the right leg and 18% towards right hand and it is found that the claimant's intellectual functioning is impaired and has low level of memory functioning.
Therefore, prays for enhancement of compensation.

The claimant has examined 3 doctors as CW- 1 to CW-3.

CW-1 is Dr. Narayana Panji, Neuro Surgeon of Nanjappa Hospital, Shivomagga, CW-2 is Dr. Batti Reddy,
ENT Surgeon of Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru and CW-3 is NC: 2024:KHC:6646 Dr. Srikanth, Ortho Surgeon of Bhagyaram Hospital, Shivomagga.

Ex .C-1 is the disability certificate of calculation of medial functions as well as physical functions of the claimant, this certificate proves that various tests were conducted on the claimant while ascertaining the disability as in detail explained and this is supported by the evidence of CW-1 to CW-3 - doctors.
As per Ex.C-2- disability certificate

,
disability suffered by the claimant is assessed at 40%.
It is an impression got by the doctors that the intellectual functioning is impaired and as low level of memory functioning and is having moderate level of disability.
The claimant summoned to the Court and directed to present before the Court.
The right hand of the claimant is completely impaired because of the fracture to the right hand and is found to be limping due to the injuries sustained to the right leg.
The claimant was constrained to give up his study at SSLC level as per the doctors evidence as above discussed, the memory functioning of the claimant is severely affected at 40%.
Where there is a 40% of disability affecting to the brain NC: 2024:KHC:6646 functions, it is a severe disability.

Therefore, the claimant has suffered both mentally and physically as per evidence of doctors and from the medical documentary evidence it is revealed that the claimant is finding difficulty in breathing while he walks for few minutes.
Therefore, where brain is affected as aforesaid all organs of the body are also affected.
Therefore, when this being the injuries and disability suffered by the claimant, then there should be is pragmatic approach to assess the quantum of compensation.
In this regard the principal of law laid down by the Supreme Court in KAJAL VS. JAGDISH CHAND AND OTHERS1 (KAJAL CASE (supra)) is the guiding factor.

.In the KAJAL CASE (supra) is the guiding factor the facts are that the claimant was 12 years old girl who has sustained 100% of disability thus the Hon'ble Supreme Court has taken notional income as per minimum wages when applicable to skilled workmen and added 30% towards loss of future prospects of life and (2020) 4 SCC 413.
NC: 2024:KHC:6646 accordingly granted the compensation of Rs.14,66,000/- under the head 'loss of income due to disability'.
10.

In the present case also the claimant was 12 years old boy suffered 43.75% of functional disability towards head injuries affecting the brain functioning and when the brain is severely affected the major functions of the body organs are affected besides the claimant has suffered fracture to the right hand and right leg.

The doctors have assessed that the claimant has suffered 19% disability towards right hand and 9% disability towards right leg even when it is evident from the doctors as discussed above that the intellectual functioning of the claimant is affected and he has lost memory.

Though the claimant has studied upto SSLC level but he was compelled to give up studies further therefore, applying the principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of RAJKUMAR VS. AJAY KUMAR AND ANOTHER2 (RAJKUMAR's case (Supra)) in order to 2011 (1)
SCC 343 NC: 2024:KHC:6646 assess the physical and functional disability and applying the principle of law laid down in KAJAL CASE (supra), this Court has followed the principle of law laid B P Manoj vs Hilari Misquith on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19864239/

11. The claimant is not able to lift his right hand as there is significant fracture on the right hand and moreover due to head injury physical functions of the claimant are affected.
Accordingly, it is justified to take 50% functional disability as discussed above.

12. Considering the accident is occurred in the year 2012, the notional income is to be taken as Rs.7,000/- per month as recognized by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority and the claimant has suffered significant (2014) 14 SCC 396 - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:6646 disability as discussed above, his future prospects is completely affected.

Therefore, according to his age 40% income has to be added towards 'loss of future prospects in life'
and the appropriate multiplier applicable is '18'.

Hence, 'loss of future earning capacity due to disability including future prospects in life' is quantified as under:
Rs.7000/- + 40% (Rs.2,800/-) = Rs.9,800/-
Rs.9,800/- x 50% x 18 x 12 = Rs.10,58,400/-
Thus, the claimant is entitled to compensation of Rs.10,58,400/- under the head 'loss of future earning capacity due to disability including future prospects in life'.
13. The compensation of Rs.2,91,893/- awarded under the head 'medical expenses' is as per actual bills produced by the claimant, which needs no interference.
Hence, same is kept intact.

14. Further, the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.50,000/- towards 'pain and suffering',
which is on lesser side.

Therefore, compensation of - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:6646 Rs.75,000/- is awarded under the head 'injuries, pain and suffering'.
15.

Further compensation of Rs.42,000/- (Rs.7,000/- x 6) is awarded under the head 'loss of income during laid up period' to the parents, as parents were looking after the claimant and they sustained 'loss of income during this period' as against Rs.5,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
16. Further, the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards food, nourishment and attendant charges, which is on lesser side.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.60,000/- is awarded towards 'food, nourishment and attendant charges'.

The impugned judgment and award dated 01.01.2019 passed by the Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kadur, Chikkamagaluru District, in MVC No.23/2013 is modified to the extent that the appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.12,03,068/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
iii. No order as to costs.
Registry is directed to transmit the TCR along with copy of this order to the Tribunal forthwith.
